text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"Daily vitamin D supplementation corrects deficiency and improves bone mineral density in adults with low baseline serum levels.","cited_pids":["vitamin_d#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"Muscle strength and fall rates improve with vitamin D supplementation in deficient populations.","cited_pids":["vitamin_d#3"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"A meta-analysis reports a modest fracture benefit in older adults when vitamin D is combined with calcium.","cited_pids":["vitamin_d#1"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"A Cochrane review found no reduction in all-cause mortality from vitamin D in adults who were not deficient at baseline.","cited_pids":["vitamin_d#5"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"The VITAL trial, with 25871 participants, found no significant effect of vitamin D on cardiovascular events or cancer.","cited_pids":["vitamin_d#4"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"Routine vitamin D supplementation in adults with adequate levels shows no measurable outcome gain.","cited_pids":["vitamin_d#6"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"High-dose vitamin D has been linked to hypercalcaemia and, in some trials, higher fall risk.","cited_pids":["vitamin_d#7"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"Observational studies linking vitamin D to immune benefits are weaker evidence than trial evidence.","cited_pids":["vitamin_d#2"]},{"cid":"c9","text":"Vitamin D testing status matters when deciding whether supplementation is worthwhile.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c10","text":"Routine daily vitamin D use for all adults is not well supported by the evidence.","cited_pids":[]}]}
